text:
jen: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: GPUs/regions/autoscale. Pulling together answers here so we can share with customers.

maria: Short summary of fallback behavior: 1) try in-region prewarmed SKUs; 2) same-region alternate SKU (quantized or smaller memory); 3) nearest healthy region (adds latency); 4) reserved/dedicated pools if customer has commit; 5) model downgrade only if customer explicitly opts into model fallbacks.

alex: Routing priorities to emphasize: capacity_hint > customer_tier > latency_slo > cost_preference. That means free-tier gets cheaper fallbacks earlier; enterprise with SLOs stays put longer.

jen: If a request switches models mid-stream, how will billing and logs show up? Customers asked for clarity.

rebecca: Billing: tokens are attributed to the model that generated them. The billing UI will display per-request token splits by model and unit price. No hidden aggregated line items.

sam: Any mitigation for sudden model switches causing incoherent output? We heard this concern often.

maria: Yes. We attempt KV/prefix cache reuse for compatible families. For incompatible switches we do a short "continuation handoff" (system-level bridge prompt, conservative sampling) and tag responses with metadata: fallback_reason and handoff=true so clients can surface this to users.

kyle: FYI ops detail: autoscaler will prefer prewarmed lanes and will only trigger cross-region routing if in-region warm capacity < threshold and latency budget allows. Example config snippet we use internally: 
```
autoscale:
  prefer_prewarm: true
  cross_region_threshold: 0.15
  latency_budget_ms: 200
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: region-fallback policy rollouts bumped to 40% by @kyle at 14:03.

jen: Action items: kyle to draft a short public FAQ paragraph about billing & fallbacks; rebecca to confirm billing UI ticket; maria to write internal doc on handoff semantics; I'll coordinate customer-facing note with comms.

rebecca: I'll paste the billing UI ticket here when it's filed.

kyle: :thumbsup: PR for FAQ by EOD.

jen: Thanks all — drop any edge-case examples here and we'll add to the FAQ.
